title: The powers of a primitive root are pairwise incongruent (Int.primitive_root_pow_injective)
statement: For n : Nat with 0 < n and a : Int a primitive root mod n -- `Int.IsPrimitiveRoot n a`, i.e. the order of a is exactly `Nat.totient n` -- the exponents below phi(n) give pairwise incongruent powers: if i, j < phi(n) and a^i = a^j (mod n) then i = j. This is the reason primitive roots are worth naming: the phi(n) powers a^0, ..., a^(phi(n)-1) enumerate the units without repetition. The proof's one interesting step is that `Coprime (a^i) n`, needed for cancellation, comes out of the ORDER RELATION itself rather than from a multiplicativity lemma the development does not have: writing t = i + f, the congruence a^i * a^f = 1 says a^f IS a modular inverse of a^i, and the Bezout extraction that turns an inverse into a coprimality was already a named helper (`coprime_of_modeq_inverse`). What this does NOT claim: this is injectivity of the power map, NOT surjectivity onto the units, and it asserts nothing about WHETHER a primitive root exists for any given n -- existence modulo a prime is not established here (ADR-1598 records the measured obstruction, the absence of a divisor-set aggregate in either prelude).

formal.statement: ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : Int) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : AxNat) -> ((x4 : AxNat.lt AxNat.zero x0) -> ((x5 : Int.IsPrimitiveRoot x0 x1) -> ((x6 : AxNat.lt x2 (AxNat.totient x0)) -> ((x7 : AxNat.lt x3 (AxNat.totient x0)) -> ((x8 : Int.ModEq (Int.ofNat x0) (Int.pow x1 x2) (Int.pow x1 x3)) -> Eq.{1} AxNat x2 x3)))))))))

evidence.supports: The definitions this statement is about compute the intended values at concrete small arguments, and the discriminating negative cases FAIL: ord_8(3) = 2 (not phi(8) = 4), ord_7(3) = 6, and 3 is refutably NOT a primitive root mod 8.
evidence.notes: The trusted gate cannot tell you a Definition is wrong -- it type-checks either way -- so Int.IsOrder and Int.IsPrimitiveRoot are pinned by reduction at concrete small arguments. Each battery asserts BOTH what must hold and what must fail, so no run can be vacuous: three_mod_eight_is_killed_by_exactly_the_even_exponents requires hits at m in {0,2,4} and misses at {1,3,5} (the misses are the negative control for Int.pow_modeq_one_of_dvd); is_order_unfolds_to_the_intended_conjunction requires the definition to be def_eq to the intended conjunction and NOT def_eq to the variant with the positivity comparison transposed; three_has_multiplicative_order_two_mod_eight builds a witness for IsOrder 8 3 2 and a REFUTATION of IsOrder 8 3 4, which only the minimality conjunct separates. Confirm a NONZERO test count (6).

provenance.prior_art: Classical; Gauss, Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801), art. 52-57. The injectivity half only; Gauss's theorem that a primitive root exists modulo every prime is NOT part of this fact.

notes: Roadmap item W1-7 (docs/math-department/00-roadmap.md), the number theorist's first Next Five entry. ADR-1598 records why the order is a PREDICATE picked out by bounded search rather than a Nat-valued function, and what did not land: existence of a primitive root modulo a prime, whose measured obstruction is that the standard counting route needs sum over d | n of phi(d) = n and neither prelude has a divisor-set aggregate.
